children: is set to face a California court over allegations that Black workers at its Fremont assembly plant were subjected to widespread racial harassment and unequal treatment, adding to a series of discrimination cases involving the electric vehicle maker.
The California Civil Rights Department's lawsuit, filed in 2022, alleges workers encountered racial slurs and graffiti and that Tesla
failed to adequately address the conduct. The agency also accuses the company of paying Black employees less and limiting their access to promotions.
The case goes before state Superior Court Judge Peter Borkon in Oakland on Monday, with proceedings scheduled through October 30. Borkon will decide the case in a bench trial rather than a jury.
has denied wrongdoing and said it does not tolerate discrimination, adding that it has dismissed workers found to have engaged in misconduct.
California law does not place a cap on damages for workplace discrimination, meaning Tesla
could face damages totaling millions of dollars if found liable.
The agency's allegations extend beyond harassment, claiming the Fremont facility was racially segregated and that Black workers were concentrated in lower-paying, less desirable positions.

also faces a racial-harassment lawsuit from the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and dozens of individual cases. In one such case, a former Fremont worker received a $137 million jury award that was later reduced by a judge.
Shares were trading around 4% higher on Monday.

title: Tesla heads to trial over California claims of racial discrimination
